nvidia_primary_documentation.summary: nanosleep is approximate. Its permitted sleep interval is [0,2*t], so there is no positive minimum equal to t. Warp implementation may shorten individual sleeps; maximum sleep is1ms.
__nanosleep(ns) specifies an approximate nanosecond sleep, with approximately1ms maximum per call.

conclusions: The configured value5000 is a request expressed through5000 approximate nanosleeps; it is not proof of an actual5ms delay.

The enclosing host intervals include the real profiler call and its final stream synchronization. They do not support a claim that a full5ms delay completed on that synchronized stream during those calls.
The native delay and event profiler resolve current streams through different APIs. A stream mismatch is a concrete hypothesis, not demonstrated by saved stream handles or a delay trace.

The following correctness routine begins with device-wide synchronization. Its >=5.168ms post-return interval is consistent with outstanding work outside the profiled stream; it also includes numerical operations and substantial first-use overhead, so it is not an isolated measurement of delay or synchronization.
Saved traces were captured only for later retained-graph replays; their absence of delay events cannot establish absence of delay execution during earlier profiling.
Neither the short host durations nor the approximate nanosleep contract identifies the cause of the candidate-ranking reversal. Do not label existing auto timing as proven host-overhead-free.

tvm_ffi_stream_review.provenance_limit: Official source is pinned for this review but is not proven identical to the installed package. Its __init__.py hash differs from the recorded runtime package; no historical compiled call-wrapper source/hash was saved. These semantics corroborate a concrete hypothesis, not an observed historical stream ID.
source_established_semantics: TVMFFIPyCallContext begins with device_type=-1 and stream=nullptr.
TVMFFIPyArgSetterInt_ converts5000 to an integer argument without modifying the device or stream context.
TVMFFIPyArgSetterDLPackExchangeAPI_ obtains current_work_stream from a non-CPU tensor producer; Torch fallback obtains torch._C._cuda_getCurrentRawStream for the tensor device.
The native call dispatcher sets TVMFFIEnvSetStream only when argument conversion detected a device; it restores the previous FFI stream after the call.
An integer-only delay call supplies no tensor-derived device/stream. With no outer FFI scope, it retains the ambient FFI stream; EnvContext::GetStream returns nullptr when unset.
TorchStreamContext.__enter__ optionally enters the Torch context, reads torch.cuda.current_stream(), and explicitly sets an FFI StreamContext; exit restores both contexts.
tvm_ffi_stream_review.application_to_saved_experiment: Exact FlashInfer delay_kernel passes only the integer delay; actual GEMM calls pass CUDA tensors. The profiler uses only torch.cuda.stream(stream), with no explicit FFI scope. Under the inspected binding semantics, GEMM tensor calls temporarily align streams and then restore ambient FFI state, so their warmups do not establish the same stream for the subsequent tensor-free delay call.
tvm_ffi_stream_review.required_invariant: To guarantee a tensor-free native helper follows a custom PyTorch stream under this binding model, establish the corresponding FFI stream context explicitly (for example use_torch_stream), pass an explicit native stream, or provide an equivalent guaranteed binding mechanism. Merely entering torch.cuda.stream does not itself set FFI context.
